title: Mosaic crochet rectangle shawl
subtitle: Two-colour geometric patterning in DK using back-loop-only double crochet on a 4 mm hook
excerpt: Mosaic crochet builds geometric colourwork by working back-loop-only stitches in a contrast yarn to lift a column of colour from the previous row. This rectangle shawl measures 175 cm wide by 55 cm deep in DK weight on a 4 mm hook. Two colours of yarn, one row at a time, produce a graphic repeat without ever carrying yarn across the row.
sourceNotes: Mosaic crochet technique synthesised from established BLO colourwork principles. The back-loop-only row method for two-colour geometric patterns is documented in Weldon's Practical Crochet (1886) derivatives and in the wider fibre arts canon. No single prior source.
heroPrompt: A rectangular crochet shawl in charcoal and cream DK yarn folded on a pale linen surface. The geometric mosaic repeat is clearly visible in soft natural light.

glossaryTerms.definition: Working a stitch through only the back of the two loops at the top of the stitch below, rather than both loops. Leaves a visible horizontal bar on the front of the fabric and is the mechanism that creates mosaic colour lifts.

In mosaic crochet, a row worked in the contrast colour where some stitches are replaced by BLO stitches that reach down into the previous contrast row, pulling that colour up through the current main-colour row.

content.text: This rectangular shawl uses mosaic crochet to place a two-colour geometric repeat across 175 cm of DK fabric on a 4 mm hook. The method works one colour per row: on main-colour rows you work standard double crochet (UK dc, the same move US patterns call single crochet) across all stitches; on contrast rows you alternate regular dc with
BLO

dc at the pattern positions. The BLO stitch reaches through only the back loop, pulling a stitch of contrast colour up through the row above it. The result is a geometric colourwork surface with no floats and no colour-carrying across rows.

You carry the unused colour loosely up the side edge rather than fastening off after every row. Keep the carry tension consistent: too tight pulls the edge in; too loose leaves loops that catch. The pattern uses a 12-stitch repeat so any multiple of 12 plus 2 edge stitches produces a full repeat. The stated cast-on of 314 stitches gives the full 175 cm at gauge.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Colour A (main): approximately 280 g DK-weight yarn. Colour B (contrast): approximately 150 g DK-weight yarn. A 4 mm hook (US G/6). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Stitch markers. Blocking mat and pins. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

18 dc x 20 rows = 10 x 10 cm in DK yarn on a 4 mm hook, measured in the mosaic pattern after blocking. Work a swatch of at least 25 stitches across at least 24 rows in the mosaic pattern (not plain dc), block it, and measure the central 10 x 10 cm. Gauge in the mosaic pattern runs slightly tighter than plain dc due to the BLO rows drawing in.
Stitches used
ch: chain -- UK and US shared.
sl st: slip stitch -- UK and US shared.
dc: double crochet (UK) -- the same move as US "single crochet" (sc). Yarn over once, insert hook, draw up loop, yarn over, draw through both loops.
BLO dc
: double crochet through the back loop only. Works exactly as dc but the hook enters only the back of the top two loops.
Pattern
The shawl is worked flat in rows, turning at the end of each row. Colour A rows and colour B rows alternate throughout. The ch-1 turning chain does not count as a stitch in this pattern.
Foundation chain
Using colour A, ch 316. (314 working stitches plus 2 for the turning chain.)
Row 1 (right side, colour A)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in 2nd ch from hook. 1 dc in each ch across. Turn. (314 sts)
Row 2 (wrong side, colour A)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in each st across. Drop colour A to the side (do not fasten off). Turn. (314 sts)
Row 3 (right side, colour B -- mosaic row)
Join colour B. Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). *1 dc in each of next 6 sts, 1
BLO dc
in each of next 6 sts*; repeat from * to * to last 2 sts. 1 dc in each of last 2 sts. Drop colour B to side. Turn. (314 sts)
Row 4 (wrong side, colour B)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in each st across. Drop colour B to side. Turn. (314 sts)
Row 5 (right side, colour A -- mosaic row)
Pick up colour A. Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). *1
BLO dc
in each of next 6 sts, 1 dc in each of next 6 sts*; repeat from * to * to last 2 sts. 1 dc in each of last 2 sts. Drop colour A. Turn. (314 sts)
Row 6 (wrong side, colour A)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in each st across. Drop colour A. Turn. (314 sts)
Rows 7 to 110 -- full repeat
Rows 3 to 6 form the four-row
mosaic repeat

. Continue repeating rows 3 to 6 until the work measures 55 cm from the foundation chain, ending with a completed colour A wrong-side row. At 20 rows per 10 cm the shawl reaches 55 cm after approximately 110 rows total. Fasten off both colours and weave in ends.
Finishing

Weave all ends in on the wrong side, working along the backs of several stitches in different directions so they sit flat and will not work loose. Wet-block by soaking in cool water for 10 minutes, pressing excess water out in a towel without wringing, then pinning to the stated dimensions on a blocking mat. Allow to dry completely before removing pins.
Care
Handwash in cool water with a mild wool or fibre wash. Do not tumble-dry. Lay flat on a clean towel, ease to shape, and leave until dry.
What to try next

Once you can read the BLO column positions confidently, try designing your own mosaic repeat on graph paper: each pair of rows is one design row, and the BLO positions in row 3 map to the contrast columns in the finished fabric. A corner-to-corner construction uses the same BLO principle in a diagonal format. Working the rectangle in lace-weight yarn on a 3 mm hook produces a finer, more translucent fabric from the same repeat.
